command: You write realistic test requests that software developers type to an AI coding assistant. Answer with JSON only.
system: You write realistic test requests that software developers type to an AI coding assistant. Answer with JSON only.
prompt:
The coding assistant is used by developers who build AI agents in Python with Google's Agent Development Kit, usually hosted on Google Cloud. Their requests may or may not mention that stack.

Here is one kind of help the assistant can give:

<brief>
A developer needs an agent to return data in a fixed machine-readable shape, but it sometimes answers with chatty text, wraps the data in markdown, or produces something that fails parsing. Separately or together, they must decide which Gemini model version and settings to use (how much reasoning, how much randomness), cope with a model version being retired, or switch to a backup model automatically when the main one is unavailable.
</brief>

Write three requests a developer might type to the assistant:
- two that need exactly this kind of help;
- one that sounds related but actually needs a different kind of help.

Write as real developers do: vary the tone (terse, chatty, frustrated, formal); make some vague and some full of detail that does not matter; mention their own project, code or deadline where natural. Do not reuse the wording of the brief. For the third request, say in plain words what kind of help it actually needs instead.

Answer with JSON only, in exactly this shape:
{"requests": [
 {"kind": "fits", "text": "..."},
 {"kind": "fits", "text": "..."},
 {"kind": "elsewhere", "text": "...", "needs_instead": "..."}
]}
